gate: Direction C (connector/domain-I concave patch) pre-pilot validation

gate_1_crossreactivity.question: Is the patch flavivirus-conserved (cross-reactivity/false-positive risk) or dengue-specific?
gate_1_crossreactivity.verdict: PASS — patch is dengue-specific (7-8/8 within DENV, only 2-4/8 in other flaviviruses). Low predicted Zika/WNV/JEV/YFV cross-reactivity.
gate_1_crossreactivity.caveat: Sequence-level screen. A folded-epitope cross-reactivity risk cannot be fully excluded without structural NS1 comparison, but the divergence at key contact positions (154 E->L/Q, 183 L->V/I, 198 M->L/P, 218 I->G/L) is substantial.

gate_2_interface_geometry.question: Do the 8 residues form a single coherent paratope-sized surface?
gate_2_interface_geometry.verdict: PASS — single contiguous patch, 20.5 A span, 664 A^2, matches a single nanobody paratope footprint (~15-25 A, ~600-900 A^2).

pan_serotype_note: Only position 63 varies within DENV (L in D1/D2/D4, M in D3) - conservative. Other 7 positions identical across all four serotypes.
overall_verdict: BOTH GATES PASS. Direction C is scientifically sound as a target: dengue-specific (low cross-reactivity), pan-serotype conserved, single paratope-sized concave surface. Cleared to proceed to a small binder pilot.
remaining_unknown: Designability (pass rate) is STILL unmeasured. Geometry is favorable (more concave than beta-ladder) but only a pilot run through the RFantibody pipeline can measure whether it yields passing designs (pAE < 5).
epitope_type_caveat: Conformational, discontinuous epitope (61-63/154/180-183/198/218). Valid only on correctly folded native NS1; will not present on denatured antigen. Compatible with a native-capture biosensor.
